📊 Audit Trail

Structured write audit with OpenTelemetry-compatible metrics, a pluggable sink interface, and zero overhead when disabled.

Overview

BLite 5.0.0 introduces a built-in audit subsystem that records every write (insert, update, delete) with the caller context. The audit trail is:

  • Pluggable — attach any IBLiteAuditSink implementation (database, file, HTTP webhook…)
  • OTel-compatible — BLiteDiagnostics.ActivitySource emits spans that propagate to Jaeger, Grafana, Datadog, etc.
  • Zero-overhead when disabled — the hot path is a null-sink guarded by a single bool check.

Enabling the Audit Sink

using BLite.Core.Audit;

using var engine = new BLiteEngine("mydb.blite");

engine.ConfigureAudit(new BLiteAuditOptions
{
    Sink           = new MyAuditSink(),    // your IBLiteAuditSink implementation
    EnableMetrics  = true,
    SlowOperationThreshold = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(100)
});

Custom Audit Sink

Implement IBLiteAuditSink to forward events to any backend:

// IBLiteAuditSink methods are synchronous — queue async work internally if needed
public class PostgresAuditSink : IBLiteAuditSink
{
    public void OnInsert(InsertAuditEvent e)
    {
        // e.CollectionName, e.DocumentSizeBytes, e.Elapsed, e.UserId, e.TransactionId
        _channel.Writer.TryWrite(("insert", e.CollectionName, e.UserId, DateTime.UtcNow));
    }

    public void OnCommit(CommitAuditEvent e)
    {
        // e.CollectionName, e.PagesWritten, e.WalSizeBytes, e.Elapsed, e.UserId
        _channel.Writer.TryWrite(("commit", e.CollectionName, e.UserId, DateTime.UtcNow));
    }
}

Caller Context

Use IAuditContextProvider to attach a per-request identity (e.g. the current HTTP user) to every audit entry:

public class HttpUserContextProvider : IAuditContextProvider
{
    private readonly IHttpContextAccessor _http;
    public HttpUserContextProvider(IHttpContextAccessor http) => _http = http;

    public string? GetContext() =>
        _http.HttpContext?.User.Identity?.Name;
}

// Register in DI
services.AddSingleton<IAuditContextProvider, HttpUserContextProvider>();

Engine Metrics

BLiteMetrics is updated atomically after every write and exposes counters readable without I/O:

var metrics = engine.AuditMetrics;
Console.WriteLine($"Inserts:             {metrics.TotalInserts}");
Console.WriteLine($"Index-scan queries:  {metrics.TotalQueriesIndexScan}");
Console.WriteLine($"BSON-scan queries:   {metrics.TotalQueriesBsonScan}");
Console.WriteLine($"Full-scan queries:   {metrics.TotalQueriesFullScan}");
Console.WriteLine($"Commits:             {metrics.TotalCommits}");

BLite.Server exposes these via the GET /api/v1/{dbId}/metrics REST endpoint.

OpenTelemetry Spans

When an OpenTelemetry ActivitySource listener is attached, BLite emits spans for every engine operation. Use the standard OTLP pipeline:

// In your OTLP setup
tracerProvider.AddSource(BLiteDiagnostics.ActivitySource.Name);

BLite.Server is pre-wired to emit spans via TelemetryInterceptor for every gRPC call. Configure the OTLP exporter in appsettings.json:

"Telemetry": {
  "Enabled": true,
  "ServiceName": "blite-server",
  "Otlp": { "Endpoint": "http://localhost:4317" }
}
